title: Running a Module in the Host
statement: Let six finite Boolean Turing machines be given, padded to a common work-tape count $K$; choose a module index $i\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$ whose machine has positive work-tape count. Let $x,\mathrm{arg},\mathrm{result},\mathrm{out},\mathrm{pre}$ be Boolean words and $q$ a state of module $i$. Suppose the module started on input $x$ at its entry configuration with argument word on tape zero and all other tapes blank stays unhalted at every time $v<t$, and at time $t$ reaches its halted configuration with state component absent, tape zero holding $\mathrm{result}$, all other tapes blank, and output $\mathrm{out}$. Then the host started at module $i$'s entry on input $x$, with the same argument word and output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$, never reaches the loop-anchor state at any time $v<t$; at time $t$ it is in module $i$'s return state with tape zero holding $\mathrm{result}$, all other tapes blank, and output $\mathrm{pre}\,\mathrm{out}$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a family of six finite Boolean Turing machines
each machine's work-tape count is at most $K$
the module is unhalted at every time $v<t$ from its canonical argument configuration
at time $t$ the module reaches the specified halted configuration with output $\mathrm{out}$
replaced:
Let the $i$-th module (with positive tape count), started at its own entry over
the state word of an argument, stay live before time $t$ and halt at time $t$
over the state word of a result with output $o$. Then the host, started at that
module's entry over the same argument with output prefix $p$: (i) never visits
the loop anchor before time $t$, and (ii) at time $t$ reaches the module's
return state over the state word of the result with output
$p \mathbin{+\!\!+} o$.
